title: RAW UNREVIEWED: one fixed alphabet ring writes the distance from the last decoded unit
summary: A complete artificial hand-writing lesson preserves ordinary open source words, their order, punctuation and paragraph scope. One fixed22-position ring writes the clockwise difference between consecutive expanded source units. The reader cumulatively adds those differences. One remembered unit replaces a changing alphabet or word dictionary. Only the first sign of a source word depends on entry; its complete inner difference sequence is fixed. No native values, source encoding, statistical fit or experiment is claimed.

design.purpose: Write meaningful ordinary text without a separate semantic-root dictionary, a phrase-ID table, a learned whole-word lexicon, or twenty-six independently changing letter states. This is a public reversible notation, not an effective secrecy claim. The source language supplies meanings; the ring preserves them without interpreting pronouns, negation, comparisons, conditions or unknown names.
design.input_domain: One or more explicitly separated paragraphs, each containing nonempty tokens over exactly lowercase a-z and the56 listed additional characters. Source tokens are separated by one space. Repeated whitespace and original physical lineation are outside this normalized input contract, as in935; spelling, case, all listed punctuation, word order and paragraph boundaries are inside it. There is no additional lowercasing, translation, stemming or grammatical normalization. Any unlisted character is a declared unsupported input, never deleted or silently replaced.
design.working_atom_assumption: The22 named existing drawings are treated as distinct atomic working signs for this invented lesson. Digraph-looking transcription names such as ch and cth denote one working drawing. This is not a claim that native atoms or group boundaries have been identified. Printed spaces correspond one-for-one to source spaces under this contract.

plain_unit_ring.indices_0_to_20: a b c d e f g h i j k l m n o p q r s t u
plain_unit_ring.index_21: ESC, a control unit rather than an ordinary source letter
plain_unit_ring.ordinary_rule: Each lowercase a-u becomes its alphabetic index0-20, one expanded source unit.
plain_unit_ring.escape_rule: For zero-based index j in this61-character list, expand the source character to exactly three units:21, floor(j/21), j mod21. Both selectors are in0-20. Thus v=21,0,0; w=21,0,1; x=21,0,2; y=21,0,3; z=21,0,4. A selector is a numerical unit inside an escape, not a separately decoded source letter. Every one of the three units participates in the ring update.
plain_unit_ring.inverse_expansion: Read a unit0-20 as its one ordinary letter. Read21 followed by exactly two units b,c in0-20 as escape index21*b+c; require index<61. Reject a trailing/incomplete escape,21 in a selector, an unused index, or an escape straddling a visible word space. There is no escaped alternative for ordinary a-u, so expansion is canonical and prefix-free.
plain_unit_ring.inventory_provenance: The56 characters after v-z are exactly the ordered rare inventory already printed in HUMAN_SOURCE_MULTIGRAPH_SHORTHAND_RAW_20261005.json (IDEA935) and used in1180/1197. This contract reuses that bounded source alphabet, not935's shortcuts or carrier. No Unicode-codepoint machinery, unprinted character registry or new corpus is introduced.

design.start_and_boundaries: At the beginning of every visibly separated source paragraph set p=0. A blank line separates output paragraphs and makes that reset public; EOF closes the last paragraph. Ordinary physical line wraps occur only between complete written groups and count as the same source space. Single spaces and ordinary line wraps do not update or reset p. Sentence punctuation is encoded like any other supported character and does not reset p. No per-word seed, arbitrary line reset or hidden restart is allowed. Very long words remain whole; their paper/line-width burden is not solved by an invisible continuation rule.
encode: Expand the next source character by the fixed ordinary/escape rule. Keep its token boundary; no substring shortcut or whole-word lookup is used.
For each expanded unit u, compute delta=(u-p) mod22 in the range0-21. By hand this is the number of clockwise steps from p to u around the fixed ring; equal positions require zero steps.
Write output_glyphs_by_distance_0_to_21[delta] and move the remembered position to p=u. ESC and its selectors obey the identical rule.
At each source word space write one visible group space without changing p. At the explicit paragraph boundary begin a new paragraph and reset p=0.
decode: Start p=0 at the public paragraph boundary. For every working glyph look up its distance delta in the one fixed22-sign order.
Move delta clockwise steps from p and recover u=(p+delta) mod22; set p=u. Parse the recovered unit stream with the fixed ordinary/escape rule.

Each visible written group must end at a complete source-character boundary. Restore its space literally. Punctuation and case come only from the ordinary/escape table, never from a guess about the sentence.
Reject malformed expanded characters. No source dictionary, original message, preferred interpretation, alternate reset or per-occurrence value is consulted.
design.reading_uniqueness: Given the fixed ring, public p=0 reset and visible groups, each glyph determines exactly one next unit. The canonical prefix-free source expansion then determines exactly one source character sequence. This proves recovery for every finite admitted input, not just the example. It does not identify an unknown Voynich ring or language. Ring/letter values are supplied teaching conventions.
design.paid_human_work: The learner knows ordinary source-language vocabulary and spelling, consults the22-position ring with its22 distance-to-glyph pairs, and learns or consults the61 escaped characters in three rows of21 cells (last row partly empty). Lowercase a-u need only the ordinary alphabetic order; v-z require the five declared escapes. The persistent message state is one position p, not26 ticks, a26-item reorderable list or a word-history dictionary. Counting requires a temporary number0-21. While decoding an escape, the reader also remembers whether zero/one/two selectors are pending and the first selector; that small parser state is explicitly additional. Up to21 steps and a glyph lookup per expanded unit may be slow. Every escaped source character costs three glyphs, every ordinary a-u one; spaces and visible paragraph separators cost written layout. No speed, historical use or total learning-time claim is made.
design.unknown_words_and_definitions: Every previously unseen token over the82 supported characters uses precisely the same expansion and distance rule. A genuinely unfamiliar concept remains an ordinary written name; its explanation, if needed, must be written as ordinary text and paid in full. The cipher adds no definition, semantic identity or antecedent. There is no fixed-length word ceiling or codebook entry for a whole message.
design.scope_and_repetition: All original lexical and grammatical scope is retained because the complete source words and their order return exactly. A repeated source letter or word is never silently erased, converted to plural, merged, or assigned an iteration meaning. The same source word can have different entry signs at different positions. Consecutive equal source words have identical second-and-later rendered forms, since each occurrence leaves the same last expanded unit. The first may also match when its incoming p already equals that final unit. Thus there is no obligatory shared repeat header. Different source words can legitimately produce the same written group at different public entry states.
necessary_shape_consequences: For a fixed source word U=(u1,...,um), only its first distance u1-p depends on the predecessor. Its entire tail (u2-u1,...,um-u[m-1]) is invariant. All entry forms have the same glyph length and differ in at most the first glyph. This is a necessary, falsifiable consequence, not claimed native support.

At a complete word boundary p is never21: a complete source character ends in an ordinary unit or a non-ESC selector. Therefore a fixed source word has at most21 entry spellings, not22 arbitrarily chosen aliases. Internal ESC still uses all22 ring positions.

Consecutive equal expanded units force delta0, the single teaching glyph a. This concerns expanded units; an escaped source character occupies three units and must not be treated as one ordinary letter in that lemma.

The sum of all distances in a group equals its last unit minus its incoming p modulo22. Identical written groups from two equal-length unit sequences U,V are possible exactly when V-U is one constant offset at every unit and the incoming states differ by that same offset; both expansions must also be legal. This allows contextual merging as well as entry splitting, unlike ALT's per-letter aliases.

Source spaces do not alter the distance stream. Joining or separating source tokens changes the written spaces but not their glyph sequence, provided each original boundary falls between complete characters. The spaces still preserve different source word boundaries; they are not semantically disposable.

There is no fixed group size, mandatory final marker, universal two-ending restriction or forced common repeat prefix. Short groups and whole repeated groups are admitted by the grammar, but this does not establish any actual native grouping or value.

The fixed public glyph order contains no qo rule and no special y ending. Native q/o concentration, final forms, long-word spread, frequency, entropy and adjacency obligations remain entirely untested. No row, state, rare list, ring order, alphabet permutation or exception will be changed after seeing a result under this card.

complete_invented_example.meaning_status: An invented ordinary German instruction: add/give the fictive named item nara to the contextually referenced destination. The destination is no more resolved than in the source. These artificial cipher spellings assign no value to any native Voynich word.
complete_invented_example.hand_readback: Starting0, q/e/f add6,2,15 modulo22 and recover6,8,1 = gib. Continue from1: k/r/sh/d add12,9,17,5 and recover13,0,17,0 = nara. Continue from0: i/cth/cfh/o/n/ch/o/o/cth recover3,0,21,0,4,20,21,0,19. Escape index4 is z; index19 is period. Read d+a+z+u+period = dazu. Both source spaces and the paragraph assumptions remain explicit. This trace was worked by hand; no encoding program, source corpus or target was executed.

design.smallest_decision_changing_consequence: If root selects a source-forward check, equality/type/top-ten/adjacent-identical partitions of these fixed numeric distance words are invariant under every global bijective renaming of the22 output drawings. A necessary failure can stop this precise source/ring contract before any palette optimization; a nonfailure only permits later inspection of the unchanged full writer. The source sequence and reset policy must already be fixed, with all exposure retained. Manual reversibility itself is not the research decision, and a near-repetition census alone is not new semantic evidence.
design.failure_and_error_costs: A wrong distance normally shifts subsequent recovered units by a constant modulo22 until the next public paragraph reset; the escape parser may then also fail. One cannot repair that by silently resetting at a convenient word. An erased space changes lexical boundaries without changing arithmetic. Many natural words may become too long due to v-z and rare-character escapes; inner-frequency or q/y conditions may fail. The fixed ordinary alphabet order is an overt construction choice, not evidence for Latin or German in Voynich. Full source coverage is bounded to the82-character teaching edition.

predecessors_and_duplicate_boundaries.boundary: The old native inverse encodes each observed source-sign pair under a word-reset preceding-observed-sign context, then learns650 mappings into a historical character language model. It failed and remains closed. This new forward rule retains one previous decoded expanded-plaintext unit across spaces and uses a fixed cyclic subtraction law, no650 independently learned rows or inverse key search. This is a related contextual cipher family, not a claim that differential writing is historically new.

All six forward learned class/position tables failed. They use97 units including15 source multigraphs,2/3/4 prior-character classes and learned per-class alphabets. This fixed ring has82 literal source characters expanded over22 units, no shortcut and one algebraic law. The old failures are not rescored or repaired, and the larger effective context alone is not evidence of success.

237 already explains a modular differential toy and warns that any text can be re-encoded. Its equation makes the next visible group a previous-visible-group-plus-message state; this card emits the difference of successive decoded plaintext units. The algebraic family is related and not newly discovered. Only a complete distinct supplied forward lesson and its fixed consequences are retained; no priority from reversibility, compression or context resemblance.

ALT stores26 ticks; MTF stores a changing26-letter list. This ring stores one previous unit, updates also through rare escapes, and has fixed22 numeric emissions. The fixed-carrier frequency-invariance argument applies, but neither old state sequence is reused. Both later negative decisions remain, no native inverse revival.

Only the pre-existing56 rare-character inventory and normalized-space source domain are reused. No16-substring table, greedy abbreviation, or static wordwise carrier is used. Its word-frequency invariance and1202's at-most-two-word-alias bound are not silently claimed to test this21-entry-state merging/splitting rule.

No previous-word prefix copying, shortest lexicon prefix, fragment cache, two-role content tuple, function-word regrouping, or iterated semantic head. The known original failures and947's later1216 direct-application stop remain; this is not a repair of their carriers or arities.
